The raw powders (purity > 99.5 wt.%) with different compositions were mixed and ball-milled in a stainless steel ball mill tank. The mass ratio of stainless steel ball: powder was 10:1 and the ball mill was operated at 150 rpm for 8 h.

The milled powders were then sintered by using SPS (D25/3, FCT, Rauenstein, Germany). The powders were heated to 700 °C without pressure, and then the temperature was further increased to 1700 °C by applying pressure of 30 MPa; the holding time was 10 min. The heating rate during the entire sintering process was 100 °C/min. Throughout the sintering process, the high-purity argon gas charged into the furnace as a protective atmosphere to prevent oxidation.
